correctedState: CONFIRMED, with two scope narrowings that do not rescue it. Our `.mcp.json` reader (packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:89-177) and the Claude plugin adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1040) each accept a closed transport set and neither maps `streamable-http` to `http`. A project or plugin `.mcp.json` entry copied verbatim from an MCP server's own documentation is parsed to null, logged as `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config` (project-config.ts:211) or as the adapter diagnostic `Claude MCP server requires a command (stdio) or url (http/sse/ws).`, and never reaches the pool - verified by running the parser, not only by reading it. Narrowing 1: of the three JSON surfaces the doc sentence names, only `.mcp.json` exists in this fork; `~/.claude.json` and `claude mcp add-json` are Claude Code CLI surfaces this rebranded fork does not ship, so the affected surfaces are project `.mcp.json`, plugin-bundled `.mcp.json`, and inline plugin manifest MCP maps. Narrowing 2: on the Claude backend only - off by default via NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE - claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`, so the Claude Agent SDK additionally reads project `.mcp.json` through its own loader, which does honour the alias; our pool still drops it, and the default Pi backend has no such fallback. Fix is a one-line alias normalization applied at both readers (and, for consistency, the Codex adapter at codex.ts:905), mapping `streamable-http` to `http` before the transport switch.
